Chapter 9: Measuring Impact—Tracking Results and Refining the System
Let’s talk about something that keeps open-book management alive and kicking—measuring its impact.
It’s not just about watching the financials. If you really want open-book management to work, you’ve got to track how it’s affecting engagement, innovation, and the overall culture too.
So, how do you know if things are on the right track? Well, it all starts with picking the right metrics. Think about financial performance—maybe you’re looking at profit margins, cash flow, cost savings, or revenue growth. But don’t stop there.
How about employee engagement? Are people sticking around longer? Are they joining in on huddles and training sessions? Simple surveys, retention rates, or even just counting participation can tell you a lot.
And then there’s innovation. You might track the number of new ideas that actually get put into action, or how many process improvements happen over time. Even feedback from customers can be a goldmine.
Here’s something to pay attention to: look for both the hard numbers and the stories behind them. Maybe after rolling out open-book management, you notice fewer people are leaving, and more are volunteering for cross-functional projects. Or, maybe those regular team huddles spark a bunch of small process tweaks that add up to some serious savings.
Regular reviews—whether you do them every quarter or once a year—make it possible to see what’s working and where things need a little nudge. And these reviews work best when everyone has a voice, from the front line all the way up.
If an incentive isn’t really inspiring people, or if a metric is pushing folks in the wrong direction, don’t be afraid to tweak the system. It’s all about staying flexible.
Think of it like tending a garden. You plant some seeds—maybe that’s a new practice or idea—then you watch what grows, and you adjust your care as the seasons change. The goal isn’t to “set and forget.” Instead, you’re nurturing a living, breathing system that adapts as your organization does.
So, here’s the key takeaway: when you make measurement and reflection part of your routine, open-book management doesn’t get stale. It keeps on fueling energy, learning, and improvement, rather than becoming just another set of rules to follow.
